endpoints.name: historical_card_registration
endpoints.notes: First-party X2 Utility fresh activation used this retired vendor endpoint; no current host or offline replacement is claimed.

cloud.failure_mode: Fresh historical activation and vendor-cloud photo delivery are unavailable. An already-configured card can still use the local receiver documented here.
cloud.notes: Set upsyncallowed=false in a local-only receiver; it must never authorize onward upload to a third party.
cloud.vendor_service: Eye-Fi / Keenai activation and upload services (retired)

identity.notes: Use the configured card identity, not a logged owner address in examples; the test vectors use documentation-range addresses.

discovery.none: There is no established Bonjour, SSDP or outbound discovery exchange. The card connects to its configured receiver. A receiver learns the card address from the incoming TCP session and identity from StartSession; direct-mode SSID scanning finds only the card's AP, not the upload target. Historical multicast/UDP configuration exists but is not a proven service.

identification.notes: Mobi direct mode uses SSID `Eye-Fi Card ` (including the trailing space) plus the last six card-MAC hexadecimal digits, WPA2 with the card's activation code, and DHCP supplied by the card. Keep the suffix and activation code private. This SSID does not reveal the receiver address.

device.name: Eye-Fi X2 / Mobi / Mobi Pro Wi-Fi SD Cards
device.notes:
Already-configured Eye-Fi cards can push photographs to a local receiver without the retired cloud. DIRECTION MATTERS: the CARD connects to a phone, computer, router or NAS listening for cleartext HTTP/SOAP on TCP 59278. This is not an outbound camera API and offers no shutter, delete, format or firmware-control command. identify_only is deliberate: this project's app has no secure Eye-Fi receiver transport, so the YAML documents a host implementation rather than pretending the mobile app can poll a card.
A card must already know its network and receiver destination, or have a working direct-mode configuration. Historical fresh X2 activation called the vendor registration service, so this document does NOT rescue a reset card by itself. Do not infer the opposite either: configured cards can still use a local receiver after the Eye-Fi/Keenai services disappeared.
SECURITY: the legacy protocol is cleartext with reusable upload credentials, and one reviewed Mobi path uses a 16-zero-byte key placeholder. Use only an isolated direct-mode network or trusted segmented LAN; never expose TCP 59278 to the internet or public Wi-Fi. Photographs are private. A new receiver needs bounded requests, strict session state and safe TAR handling, not the historical servers' unrestricted extraction behavior.

pairing.notes: There is no Bluetooth pairing. A receiver and card must share the configured upload-key profile and complete StartSession/GetPhotoStatus credentials. A local receiver should verify the second credential in constant time, bind nonce state to card/session/item and expire it after the roll; no persistent client bond is created.

credentials.notes: WPA2 protects direct-mode join; HTTP upload credentials are reusable legacy digests, not secure modern authentication. Never commit or log owner SSIDs, activation codes, upload keys, nonces or card addresses.

factory_reset.effect: No factory-reset procedure or offline reactivation path is established. Do not erase a working card to test the retired cloud flow.

methods.basis: Public receiver/configuration implementations and vendor desktop analysis; no physical card was used.
methods.description: Back up the card, read its existing network/receiver configuration or owner upload key through the mounted-card records, then configure a fixed-address local receiver. A historical O 0x06 record may allow listener provisioning but is not hardware-verified, so no automatic listener-write recipe is claimed.
methods.name: Configured card to a new local receiver

steps.action: Back up the mounted card and obtain owner consent before reading private configuration or changing any record.
Read the existing receiver/network settings and, for X2 or Mobi Pro infrastructure mode, export the owner upload key using the mounted-card channel.
Configure a fixed-address receiver on TCP 59278 for that card identity and start with the JPEG-only single-card profile.
steps.expect: The configured card opens StartSession to the local receiver; no vendor cloud connection is needed.

methods.basis: Historical vendor app analysis establishes the direct-mode SSID/WPA2/DHCP behavior; receiver-IP selection after DHCP still needs a capture.
methods.description: Join the card's existing direct-mode network using its owner-held activation code, then run the local receiver. Do not assume a fixed card address; active/profile/global listener hints and a bounded subnet-candidate mechanism are reported, but the selected address is not established.
methods.name: Already-working Mobi direct mode

steps.action: Join SSID `Eye-Fi Card ` plus the card-specific suffix using the owner activation code; do not record either in logs.
Accept DHCP from the card and start the restricted local receiver on TCP 59278.
Wait for the card to select the receiver and begin StartSession; stop if it does not rather than scanning the whole subnet indefinitely.
steps.expect: A card-initiated HTTP session arrives at the local receiver.

methods.basis: Static analysis of first-party X2 Utility 1.1.1; the registration service is retired.

cloud.local_alternative: Yes only for a card that retains working network/receiver configuration: use the primary mounted-card route or the direct- mode alternative above. There is no known local alternative for first-time activation of a reset card.

methods.description: The historical utility's fresh-activation path called the vendor's /3/cards.json registration endpoint. That service is gone, so this is evidence about the reset-card boundary, not a usable setup route.
methods.name: Historical first-party activation

steps.action: Do not promise offline activation for a reset card; recover an existing configuration or research a replacement activation path first.

setup.notes: Receiver operation requires existing card/network configuration. The two usable routes below start from that state and are source-derived, not replayed by this project. The historical cloud method is last because it is defunct and is not a current activation answer.

rejoin.notes: Changing routers or receiver addresses requires existing direct mode or mounted-card reconfiguration, not necessarily a factory reset. The network-change and listener-write paths need owner-approved validation.

testing.notes: No physical card, photograph or over-the-air session was used by this project. Three public implementations were reviewed and their 86 offline checks, including a four-call loopback receiver and hostile archive cases, passed. Historical vendor app/desktop analysis supplements those sources; it is not hardware verification.

dfu_mode.notes: No separate update-mode network identity is established.

enter.notes: The receiver offers fwversion and the card pulls /api/firmware/<MAC>; advanced receiver-only operation, not a mobile command.

image.format: Card-requested firmware image; container and compatibility are not established
image.notes: Signed-image enforcement is reported but not tested. No image is supplied by this spec.

dfu.notes: Do not offer firmware from this documentary block without an exact card profile, valid image and interruption recovery evidence.

covers: StartSession, GetPhotoStatus, UploadPhoto and compatibility-aware roll completion
Owner-keyed X2/Mobi credential verification and single-use nonce state
Multipart TAR media reception with conservative validation and storage
Read-side mounted-card configuration export with owner consent
not_covered: Factory-reset activation, universal receiver-IP discovery and unverified network provisioning
Camera shutter/delete/format control, universal RAW/video profiles and verified interruption resume
local_access.summary: The stock card pushes photos to a local host. Implement a single-card, JPEG-only, read-only-network receiver first; this project's mobile app does not currently provide that server role.

archive_policy.initial_profile: single-card JPEG-only receiver with bounded temporary spooling
archive_policy.side_effects: Skip historical geolocation/log sidecars and do not invoke external services
archive_policy.storage: Controlled destination, exclusive creation, no overwrite of different content, remove partial output on failure

credentials.algorithm: Concatenate the specified hexadecimal strings, hex-decode them, MD5 the decoded bytes, and emit lowercase hex. Do not hash ASCII hex text.

mobi_pro_infrastructure.get_photo_status: Same formula with the real owner upload key where configured
mobi_pro_infrastructure.key_source: Mounted-card read token 0xfd on an already-configured card
mobi_pro_infrastructure.start_session: Same formula with the real owner upload key where configured

reviewed_mobi.key_source: Legacy placeholder decoded as 16 zero bytes; not a recommendation

credentials.session_policy: Bind state to card identity, session, server nonce and expected item; use single-use expiring nonces and one defined outstanding transfer per card.

firmware_delivery.mechanism: A receiver may offer fwversion; the card then requests GET /api/firmware/<MAC>.
firmware_delivery.safety: Signed-image enforcement is reported in firmware strings, but no modified image or recovery path was tested. This is card-pull, not an outbound firmware-control API.

mounted_configuration.caution: Back up first. Network changes, AP start, reboot and Mobi coverage are unverified; the reference utility also has a compiler-reported mount-path lifetime warning.
mounted_configuration.channel: Files under EyeFi/ on a mounted FAT card, not a single XML settings file
mounted_configuration.sequence_encoding: Native u32 in the reference utility, little-endian on its Linux host; do not generalize without checking the card representation.
mounted_configuration.transaction: Increment previous response sequence (seed 0x1234 if zero), write reqc, poll rspc up to 50 times at 300 ms intervals, then read rspm only on a matching fresh sequence.

sequence.local_profile: Generate a fresh 16-byte snonce, encode all 32 hex characters, and set upsyncallowed=false.
Verify the second credential in constant time and bind the expected item to this card/session.

sequence.file_content: TAR archive containing media first and an optional event log second; filesize is TAR bytes.
sequence.response: UploadPhotoResponse with Boolean success only after the request matches the authorized card/session/item, INTEGRITYDIGEST verifies against that authorized item's upload key, and storage is completely and safely finished; otherwise success=false.

sequence.compatibility: Community X2 server: empty success; reviewed Mobi server: unimplemented; historical Windows: SOAP fault 2 / Last Photo then close. Hardware evidence must choose the profile.

receiver.xml: Match operations and fields by XML local name; bound metadata and reject DTDs, external entities and duplicate fields.

resume.filesignature_algorithm: unknown; do not invent one or deduplicate on filename alone
resume.initial_implementation: offset=0 is the conservative first profile; nonzero resume needs an interruption capture

integrity_digest.algorithm: For each complete 512-byte TAR block, compute the 16-bit Internet checksum over big-endian 16-bit words with end-around carry and invert it. Serialize each inverted sum as two big-endian bytes, concatenate them in block order, append the authorized item's 16-byte upload key, MD5 the result, and emit 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
integrity_digest.coverage: Only complete 512-byte TAR blocks are hashed; exclude a trailing partial block.
integrity_digest.verification_policy: Recompute and compare INTEGRITYDIGEST using the upload key bound to the authorized card/session/item before returning UploadPhoto success.

resume.new_destination_offset: Spooled bytes rounded down to a 4 KiB boundary
